Armored Warfare VS World of Tanks

What are your guys' opinions of both games? Please give a reason why and explain your reasoning. This is an unbiased post, because I want to see what everyone thinks and whether or not it will take off.

From my point of view it seems like Armored Warfare fixes every problem I have with world of tanks and adds some more nice things.

World of Tanks Problems

Problem 1: The "Can't do shit" issue

In World of Tanks I more often than not ran into a situation where I simply could not do anything. Being thrown into higher tier matches with a stock medium, too weak to penetrate any of the enemy tanks for example.
In Armored Warfare it seems that no matter who I am up against, there is always something I can do. Some different ammo I can switch to, some ability to mark the enemy tank. Just something other than being a moving shield.

Problem 2: Matchmaking

World of Tanks has the worst matchmaking in any online game ever. Just throwing people together who are vaguely in the same tier, ignoring their loadout and the ton of stats you have about them? Why?
Armored Warfare has yet to demonstrate how well their matchmaking works, but having some kind of stat bases mm is always better than none.

Problem 3: Freemium

Premium Ammo. Need I say more? The whole concept is ridiculous. This is the point where the largest meta problem surfaces, the company Wargaming. A bunch of greedy salesman who don't care at all about their game and community as long as they still bath in money.

Problem 4: Artillery

I have yet to play an artillery in Armored Warfare, but it seems that their concept actually works for everyone involved. It is less RNG dependent and does not force people to camp, in fact it seems to discourage camping with its large area of effect.

Problem 5: UI

In WoT I always had to have a bunch of mods installed because the user interface does a terrible job at conveying information. In AW the interface is already very well laid out, showing everything I need to know.

Armored Warfare Extras

PvE

In my opinion, the PvE adds a lot more to the game than many people seem to realize. Not only is it a ton of fun to play, but it also encourages (or rather forces) people to work together.
WoT has a terrible community and I saw AWs community having a similar start ingame. All the hostility seemed to stop the moment PvE was added. Playing together with other people instead of only against them gives the community an ingame leg to stand on. Not just behind the closed doors of clans, but for everyone.

The crew system

The crew system in WoT is terribly grindy and not one bit interesting. The commander system in AW gives me a lot more incentive to train my crew and unlock their abilities. Also, having the first level up rather early gives a nice feeling of progression and success, which is overall rather absent in WoT.

Obsidian

I have never before seen such a huge amount of communication with the community in any game. Unlike with Wargaming, I believe that Obsidian really wants to build the best game possible for the community. They are well known to be a top quality studio and from what I have seen so far, they are doing all they can to have AW live up to their regular quality.

Conclusion

Of course it is too early to say if all of this will hold up in the long run and the publisher of AW is like a dark cloud on the horizon. Here is hoping that they don't fuck things up.
I had a lot more fun in the short time I have played AW than in my entire time as a WoT player and if the game continues to feel that great it might be the next big thing in competitive gaming.
Even if it is not, it puts WoT out of its monopoly position and gives players a choice. This is always a good thing and looking at Wargamings recent moves it is rather necessary by now.

Great work Obsidian, keep it up!

That kind of thing is absolutely unacceptable. It really shows that Wargaming does not care about their game or community at all. I wonder why people are so super defensive about WoT and Wargaming in forums and on reddit.

About the community of WoT; I have played more online games than I can remember and quite a few of them had bad communities. Or so I thought. Until I started to play WoT. Suddenly all the problems that the other communities had seemed to fade in comparison.
I really wonder why it is like that. It can't be just because of the competitive only factor, many games have that. What is it that makes so many WoT players behave so horrible?

What is it that makes so many WoT players behave so horrible?

As a philosopher and logical thinker, I ask myself the same question. However I will try to answer it to the best of my ability.

A few years ago, Wargaming patented a system of match making that balances the players against one another, based on the idea of favoritism. How it works, is if you have a streak of great games, obviously you're a great player. Wargaming uses this to balance the teams and throws you onto teams where you are either the best player, or one of the best players, against teams that have been doing very badly. These teams are usually "unicum" players, or are damn near close.

Essentially, World of Tanks' match maker will intentionally pair you up against a better team with players that has been loosing recently. But why have they been loosing? The patent also describes in detail what happens if you win more than what you should be. That is to say, if your overall win rate is above 50%, you will start to loose more frequently. The game will also rig your Random Number Generator Potential. have you ever had a string of games, or even an entire month where your shots have missed, you have hit the bottom of the barrel in damage rolls, and have been continually paired with bad teams? You start to see a pattern emerging and when it does, you ask yourself a few questions. "Why me?" is probably the first thing that comes out of your mouth.

They do this so that players on the enemy team can have a better chance of winning than you. Ever have a game where you get rolled and you've only done 10 damage in your top tier e100? Have you ever bounced the side of a T1 cunningham with a round that was so big that it is the size of the T1? Rigged match making is not a conspiracy. It is real, although I do not have the link to the patent, it can be found after doing some deep research.

I was willing to forgive this after some thought. I asked why they would do such a thing, as to seemingly rig the game. What happens in an FPS when you're so green, the enemy thinks you're a plant? They shoot you and they kill you, to the point where you say "Fuck this" and uninstall. Wargaming rigs the RNG and MM systems to favor the shitier players of the match, so that they play longer.

What happens when the noob gets to tier six and can't progress in three games? They buy a premium tank, premium time, and gold. So now you have a shit player in an IS-6, or god forbid a Panther 8.8 or an AMX CDC, bottom tier in a tier ten match, in a tank they have no idea how to play, against tanks they had no idea even existed. Doesn't that ruin the game for everyone involved? Perhaps, but look at it like this; to the noob, it's an amazing experience seeing the full HD e100 for the first time. Even if they do horribly, they can chalk it up to being bottom tier. So what they'll do is they'll continue their grinds until they get to tier ten, still having not learned very much.

Then what will likely happen, is they will try to play the tank, but they won't really understand it or grasp it. Perhaps it's a kid, who is off for the summer having some fun on this game. There's nothing wrong with that right? No, but when the game seriously penalized you for loosing in tier ten, you want to win, sometimes by any means necessary. All of this effort, just so you can make a profit and if you aren't running premium, forget about it, because it won't ever happen. How does the e100 feel about this? He hates it, but he's done the same thing already and doesn't want to leave a game he just paid nearly 100 dollars for, so he'll continue to play. Who wins out of this situation?

You could say it's the community and perhaps it is, but I put the blame where it's deserved; right on Wargaming. There are so many ways they can change the community and the experience, but what do they worry about? HD tanks and map reworks.
